runs.title: Audit and correct the roadmap content objective by objective
runs.summary: Human-led assessment of every objective, phase and run in roadmap.json, correcting each objective in place before moving to the next.
runs.full_description: This run is an audit: the artifact already exists, so the work is judgement rather than implementation. The execution stage is the operator's own assessment, walking the roadmap one objective at a time and judging each run against reality: whether its status reflects what actually happened, whether its description still matches the work, and whether it is duplicated, superseded, missing or misplaced. Alongside the operator's own feedback, each objective is also checked for current naming (Cantu Studio, Editor, Web Engine, Slides Engine, Project Console) and for retired certification vocabulary, preserving scope disclaimers as live guardrails while cleaning certification disclaimers as residue: where old text states something true in a dead language, the fact is preserved and the word is changed. AI assists by mapping and presenting the current content and by reviewing the corrections for consistency, but the verdict is the operator's. Findings whose verdict is already known are corrected in place within this run, through the roadmap tool rather than by hand-editing the file. A finding that needs a verdict this run cannot give, or work that does not fit an in-place content correction, becomes its own follow-up run at the moment it appears. An objective is corrected and approved by the operator before the next objective is opened. This run closes when every objective has been assessed and approved.

runs.title: Build the roadmap maintenance and follow-up insertion tool
runs.summary: Design and implement a command-line tool that inserts, moves, removes and edits roadmap runs while keeping queue_order contiguous, dependencies valid and run identity stable.
runs.full_description: Editing roadmap.json by hand is the main cost of maintaining the roadmap: every insertion resequences the whole tail, every move risks inverting a dependency, and a single off-by-one fails the validator. This run designs and builds a bounded command-line tool that performs those edits safely. It must support inserting a run before or after an existing run and at the end of a phase, moving a run to a new position, removing a run, swapping two runs, and editing a run's text fields and dependencies. After every operation it must automatically resequence queue_order so it stays unique and contiguous from one, verify that each dependency still precedes its dependents with no cycles, refuse any edit that would orphan a depends_on reference, preserve every existing run_id as a stable identity, preserve the file's byte-level encoding including its em-dashes, and run the Project Console validator as a self-check, refusing to write when the validator would fail. It writes only to the roadmap source and performs no Git action. The tool is a command-line surface: it does not add write actions to the Project Console, which stays read-only. Making the console itself editable is a separate decision that would build on this tool's core logic rather than replace it.

runs.title: Make the Project Console edit the roadmap
runs.summary: Add roadmap editing to the Project Console, reusing the command-line tool's core so the console can insert, move, remove and edit runs, phases and objectives with the same safety guarantees.
runs.full_description: The Project Console was built read-only on purpose: it renders project state and does not mutate it. This run revisits that decision for roadmap content specifically, because auditing and maintaining the roadmap through the command line is slower than doing it where the roadmap is already displayed. It adds a write path for roadmap edits only: the console gains an editing surface for runs, phases and objectives, backed by a server endpoint that imports the existing roadmap core module rather than reimplementing its logic, so every edit keeps the same guarantees - queue_order stays contiguous, dependencies still precede their dependents, no cycles, no orphaned dependencies, identity is never mutated, and the file is written atomically with the validator as the authority. The console keeps rendering everything else read-only; this run does not turn it into a control plane for the project, does not schedule work, and does not mutate any state other than the roadmap source. It supersedes the read-only boundary only for roadmap content, and the objective and foundation text that assert a fully read-only console must be updated to say so.

runs.full_description: Human QA of the console roadmap editor drove a series of usability corrections. The snapshot-load banner told the operator to serve the repo with a plain static host, which lacks the edit and history-sync endpoints; it now names serve-project-console.mjs on 8787. The insert form gained an editable Position field prefilled from the anchor, so the resulting queue_order is visible before preview instead of after. Objectives gained presentational reordering and a manual archive flag, with a collapsible Archive section at the bottom of the tree; the core refuses archiving an objective that holds an active run. Per-block preview buttons were replaced by one global Preview all changes that batches every changed field into a single dry-run, confirm and write. Objectives and phases were reduced to a title only; summary and full_description were removed from the schema, the data and the console, and remain recoverable from Git. runs.title: Make it possible to close an active run
runs.summary: Design and implement the missing route from active to completed without weakening the progress invariant or fabricating progress.
runs.full_description: There is no route from active to completed. A completed run requires every progress entry to be in state done; the console does not edit progress by design, because progress is an execution record and editing it rewrites history; and set-status refuses transitions that would need fabricated progress. The result is that RUN-CANTU-ROADMAP-CONTENT-AUDIT-001 cannot be closed at all once its assessment is finished. This run designs and implements the missing route. It must not weaken the core invariant: a completed run still may not hold a non-done progress entry, and nothing may be fabricated. Note that progress is optional in the model: a run may go planned to active to completed with no progress array, which is how the tooling runs closed. AIW is not connected, so the progress cycle is currently cost without benefit; the operator may prefer runs that carry no progress until AIW returns.

runs.title: Fix four defects in the global console renderer, and the projector mirror the tests assert against
runs.summary: Correct the Overview active-run label fallback, the missing model-cache fallback in the edit modal, and the Add run position default that asserts a false execution order.
runs.full_description: REFRAMED 2026-07-30 by the cabin's human audit, after a read-only measurement of the code. This run was written against the LOCAL console of cantu-studio during editor QA. Its defects travelled byte for byte into the global console when that console was ported, and MEASURED TODAY ALL THREE ARE PRESENT IN BOTH COPIES, none of them touched by the finishing runs, and NONE OF THEM COVERED BY ANY TEST. So this is now a run against the GLOBAL console — the live one at project-console/, the one the launcher starts, never the fork at docs/project-console/ nor the retired prototype at console/. Repairing them in the live copy is what matters; the local copy is retired by the cutover. FOUR DEFECTS, and the fourth was found by the same measurement. (A) THE OVERVIEW LABEL FALLS BACK TO THE LITERAL "Now", and the cause in the original text — that it happens when no run is active — is WRONG, which matters because it changes the repair. The real cause is a KEY-SPACE MISMATCH: the function that computes a run's queue group returns five keys, while the label table declares four and is missing ready_next and later. When a run resolves to either of those two the lookup returns undefined and the fallback fires, whatever the run's status. Measured on this project today, with zero active runs, the label produced is actually "History", because the fallback picks the first run of the queue and that one is completed — which is its own defect: a COMPLETED run painted under "Current work item". THE DECISION THE OPERATOR TOOK, which removes the only judged part of this run: when no run is active, show the NEXT ELIGIBLE run labelled "Next up", and hide the block entirely when there is none. The machinery already exists — ready_next is computed and only missing from the label table. (B) THE EDIT MODAL'S CACHE READ IS ASYMMETRIC: one function reads the model cache with a fallback and the other reads it without, so with the cache empty and the modal open the Position field renders while Preview all changes reports NO CHANGES WHEN THERE ARE. That is the worst of the four: it does not look wrong, it makes the operator conclude there was nothing to apply. (C) THE ADD RUN AFFORDANCE DEFAULTS TO END-OF-PHASE, which in an early phase produces a low queue_order asserting the run executed near the start of the project. It is not cosmetic: it pushes against the rule that governs this roadmap, that a run is inserted where it will really execute and never at the end for convenience. Its own original text records that the launchers run nearly landed at position 2 this way. (D) THE PROJECTOR'S MIRROR HAS DIVERGED. tools/projector/project.mjs declares a function to be a mirror of the console's queue-group function and no longer is: it lacks the needs_human_decision branch and the barrier branch. AND THE TESTS ASSERT AGAINST THE MIRROR, NOT AGAINST THE RENDERER — which is why defect (A) has no net. It is repaired here rather than in the suite run because it is the same function and the same key space, and separating them guarantees they diverge again.

runs.title: Add phase and objective create and delete operations
runs.summary: Add the phase and objective create and delete operations the roadmap tool lacks, so structural corrections like new phases and removed objectives do not need hand-editing.
runs.full_description: The roadmap tool implements all run-level operations, including run insert, move, remove and swap, but it has no operation to create or delete a phase or an objective. Consequences: the Project Console objective has no phase for meta-work, because its three phases predate the decision that system and console work opens a run, so the dev launchers landed in Roadmap Maintenance for want of a better home; the two ghost phases left over from the Web component regrouping cannot be deleted; and any structural correction the audit finds at the phase or objective level needs hand-editing roadmap.json, which is what the tool exists to avoid. This run adds phase and objective create and delete through the core, the shared plan, the CLI and the console, following the same pattern by which objective move and archive were added. The single unavoidable core change is extending the identity guard to accept a sanctioned added or removed phase or objective id, since it currently rejects any change to those id sets. Deletion needs a design decision the operator has not made: refuse when the phase or objective still holds children, or cascade. The existing precedent is refusal with an explicit opt-in flag, as run removal already refuses when dependents exist.

Commit + confirm a clean git log BEFORE issuing the next ticket." — written before lanes existed, so a thread reading it would keep executing serially even with the roadmap already migrated. runs.title: Publish the run classification specification and register it as a transversal decision
runs.summary: Write the classification system as a canonical document under context/ and register the transversal decision in DECISIONES.md.
runs.full_description: The system was born in the cantu-studio thread, which measured that the kind of work a run represents was not declared anywhere, and it was closed in the cockpit's human audit of 2026-07-29/30. Today it exists only as text pasted into two cabin conversations: no ticket can cite it, no run can depend on it, and the console cannot reference the derivation table it is meant to implement. This run gives it a home. WHAT IT PUBLISHES: four measured classification fields — correctness_model (SPECIFIED / JUDGED_ACCEPTS / JUDGED_DEFINES), work_type (COSMETIC / FUNCTIONAL / FOUNDATIONAL), blast_radius (LOCAL / ADJACENT / SYSTEMIC / PROJECT_SHAPE) and failure_surfaces (LOUD / VISIBLE / SILENT); one guard list, external_effects, empty by default; and two DERIVED values that are never stored, severity and closure_mode. It publishes the two derivation tables, the three illegal combinations a validator must reject, the three mechanical rules for mixed runs, and the care_budget table as per-project configuration rather than a hard rule. TWO AXES, NOT ONE, and this is the decision with the widest reach: CLOSURE is derived — what it takes to close a run — while DELEGABILITY is declared at project level: whether AIW may execute it at all. AIW's own roadmap already declares its side in writing, that every run of that roadmap is manual under the anti-self-hosting rule with aiw-console as the explicit exception. Four competing vocabularies exist for this axis across the workspace and one of them is about to be built by a planned run in AIW's roadmap; separating the two axes is what stops a fifth from being added. That separation is transversal, so it is registered in context/DECISIONES.md and executed in each thread separately. WHERE IT LIVES: a canonical document under context/, transversal because it governs all three projects; the entry in DECISIONES.md; and a pointer — not a copy — in the CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md of each repository, since those are the rules an agent reads from the repo it works in. The pointers in aiw and cantu-studio are their threads' work and are only named here. It does not go in any handoff: handoffs are ephemeral and doctrine in one is state that rots. NO FIELD IS ADDED TO THE SCHEMA HERE and no run is classified here. This run is paper. The schema is the next one, and classification the one after that.

runs.title: Make the test suite stable under change — assert against fixtures, not live sibling data
runs.summary: Move the suite's assertions off live sibling data and onto fixtures, so a green suite means the code works rather than that the neighbours have not changed.
runs.full_description: MEASURED BY THE AIW THREAD on 2026-07-29 and reported to this one, not verified here: 278 tests, 268 passing, 10 FAILING. The ten are not three problems but one — every one of them asserts against LIVE, MUTABLE data instead of a fixture. Five fail because cantu-studio grew from 71 to 73 runs; two because that project's reviewed document count moved from 38 to 45; three because this repository's own O0 no longer holds an active run and therefore derives in_progress rather than active. None of those is an invariant. Repainting the numbers would be green today and red the day any neighbour moves, and the cabin's human audit is about to move all of them. WHY IT IS FIRST IN THE QUEUE, and there are four independent reasons. It is the arbiter of the schema change that follows: adding fields to the roadmap on top of a suite with ten inherited failures makes a real regression indistinguishable from the existing rot. AIW's roadmap holds a planned run that needs a large repository WITH A TEST NET as its first real target, and this repo is the natural candidate — the exception is written in AIW's own canonical, that runs targeting aiw-console are delegable to the kernel — but it cannot serve as the arbiter of a run that modifies the very data the suite asserts against. The classification system makes a run's failure surface a first-class field, and the LOUD value is an assertion about infrastructure rather than about the run: labelling anything LOUD while the suite is red is a false promise, and LOUD is the value that LOWERS severity, so a red suite systematically under-classifies. And the run that repairs the console defects needs to know whether its repair broke anything. SCOPE: move the assertions onto fixtures and leave, over the real sibling projects, only a smoke test that they load. A SECOND PATTERN, MEASURED IN THIS REPOSITORY AND WIDER THAN THE TEN: tests/roadmap.test.mjs and tests/roadmap-emitted.test.mjs assert against roadmapQueueGroup in tools/projector/project.mjs, which declares itself a mirror of the console's v3QueueGroupKey and has diverged from it. A suite that asserts against a mirror goes green over a copy that no longer describes what is painted. The specific repair of that mirror belongs to the console-defects run; the pattern — assert against the thing, not against its mirror — belongs here. ALSO MEASURED AND IN SCOPE: running this suite leaves the working tree dirty, because the real-project test re-emits .project/ for real and only guarantees the canonical stays byte-identical. Running the suite is therefore not a read-only operation in this repository, which matters under parallel lanes.

runs.title: The five classification fields enter the roadmap schema, with derivation at read time and a minimal view
runs.summary: Add the five stored classification fields as optional run keys, derive severity and closure_mode at read time, and transport the derivation table in the envelope.
runs.full_description: Implements in the schema, the engine, the validator, the emitter and the console what the specification run publishes. THE SHAPE IS ALREADY SET BY PRECEDENT: the run that brought lanes and barriers into the schema did exactly this — schema, engine allowlists, invariants, emitter transport and a minimal view, all in one run — and this one copies that shape rather than inventing one. WHAT IS STORED: correctness_model, work_type, blast_radius, failure_surfaces, external_effects and classified_at. WHAT IS NEVER STORED: severity and closure_mode. They are COMPUTED AT READ TIME from the stored fields, which is the contract's own rule against persisted derivatives, the same rule under which objective and phase status are derived and never written. The payoff is that the day the derivation table improves, no data migrates. THE FIELDS ARE OPTIONAL KEYS, ABSENT BY DEFAULT, and this is load-bearing: on the day they land there are roughly 89 live runs across three projects with no classification, and a required field would make all three roadmaps invalid at once and force classification under pressure — the worst possible condition for work that needs the operator's judgement. The precedent is measured: fifty runs of cantu-studio carry no lane key at all and resolve to the declared default at read time. THE VALIDATOR REPORTS, IT DOES NOT REJECT: a live run with no classification is listed, not refused. An absent classified_at is exactly the console's to-do list, at no extra cost. WHAT THE VALIDATOR DOES REJECT are the three illegal combinations: SPECIFIED with FOUNDATIONAL, FOUNDATIONAL with LOUD, and any JUDGED_ with UNATTENDED. A field that can be saved wrong gets saved wrong. TRANSPORT: the envelope carries the vocabulary and the derivation table as a versioned executable table, and the RESULT does not travel — the same discipline already recorded for the status vocabulary. TWO OBSTACLES MEASURED BY THE CABIN AND NOT PREVIOUSLY SEEN, both of which this run must resolve or explicitly defer. First, cantu-studio's canonical declares a DIFFERENT schema_version — jame.roadmap_v3.v0.2-progress, where this repo and aiw declare roadmap_tree_v1 — so engine, validator and emitter must either accept both or that project migrates first. Second, the roadmap engine EXISTS IN TWO COPIES: this repo holds roadmap-core.mjs and roadmap-plan.mjs, while the CLI roadmap-edit.mjs still lives only in cantu-studio. If the fields land only in this repo's engine, the other copy is blind to them, and that project has by far the largest set of runs to classify. What has to change inside cantu-studio is that thread's work and is only named here. ALSO IN SCOPE: the care_budget table — the per-severity model and effort defaults — as PER-PROJECT configuration, editable from the console, with the defaults the cabin fixed. It is advice, not a rule; a single run may deviate in either direction, and the deviation travels in the ticket, not in a field.

runs.title: Classify aiw-console's live runs as the pilot, and rule on the procedure itself
runs.summary: Classify this roadmap's live runs as the first real application, and deliver a verdict on the procedure itself for the other two threads.
runs.full_description: FIRST REAL APPLICATION of the classification system, and it is deliberately a PILOT. The project's own doctrine is that a new procedure is never launched in a batch: the first application goes alone and its ticket asks for a verdict on the procedure itself — which step was not executable, what had to be interpreted, which exit criterion was missing. The measured reason is that a gap found in one place costs one session, while found in three it costs three and produces verdicts that cannot be compared, because each one resolved the gap its own way. THE DELIVERABLE IS THEREFORE DOUBLE: the live runs of this roadmap classified, and a written verdict on the procedure that the aiw and cantu-studio threads start from instead of rediscovering. WHY THIS ROADMAP IS THE PILOT: it holds the smallest live set of the three, it is the thread that implements the fields, and its live runs already have their text transcribed verbatim. THE COMPLETED RUNS ARE NOT CLASSIFIED. closure_mode routes execution and a closed run is never executed again; classifying it is archaeology with zero operational value, and across the three projects it would be roughly 59 runs of work that buys nothing. A handful of closed runs MAY be classified as calibration, chosen for that purpose and declared as such. THIS RUN IS ATTENDED BY ITS OWN CLASSIFICATION: correctness is the operator's judgement supplied as an INPUT, not accepted at the end, so it executes in the cockpit with the operator and not as delegated work. THINGS THE CABIN ALREADY MEASURED AND THAT THIS RUN SHOULD WATCH FOR: the criterion that catches runs establishing something others consume caught roughly a third of the runs in scope across the three roadmaps, so blast_radius inflation is a real risk for that third and is detected by counting; a run may hold several failure surfaces, in which case the worst one wins and, if that unfairly raises the whole run, the signal is to split it; and a precondition the operator must satisfy BEFORE a run starts does not make that run JUDGED_DEFINES — nine runs in AIW's roadmap declare they cannot execute until an entry is written, and reading those as judgement would divert nine runs away from the kernel forever.
